assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

### agent_supports: yes

Hermes Agent's single-session task-list primitive is the **`todo`** tool (Claude Code uses TaskCreate/TaskUpdate; OpenCode `todowrite`; gemini-cli `write_todos`; codex `update_plan`). The shipped source is authoritative: `tools/todo_tool.py` declares `TODO_SCHEMA = {"name": "todo", ...}` with a `todos` array whose items are `{id: string, content: string, status: string}` and `VALID_STATUSES = {"pending", "in_progress", "completed", "cancelled"}`, and registers it with `registry.register(name="todo", toolset="todo", ...)`. The module docstring states the semantics the scenario needs: "Provides an in-memory task list the agent uses to decompose complex tasks, track progress", "Single `todo` tool: provide `todos` param to write, omit to read", "Every call returns the full current list". `merge=false` (the default) is a FULL-LIST REPLACE — structurally identical to opencode's `todowrite` — and `merge=true` updates existing items by id. The schema description pins the walk the scenario asserts: "Only ONE item in_progress at a time. Mark items completed immediately when done."

The tool runs inside the agent's own turn loop (an in-memory `TodoStore` on the AIAgent instance, one per session) — it spawns no child session and writes no `parent_session_id`, so `SubagentCount` stays 0. Hermes' subagent primitive is a different tool (`delegate_task`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`), which the recipe explicitly forbids.

It is enabled by default on the surfaces this cell records: `toolsets.py:54` lists `"todo"` under "# Planning & memory" in the default CLI/messaging tool set, and again in the `coding` (`toolsets.py:362`) and `hermes-acp` (`toolsets.py:394`) toolsets. `check_todo_requirements()` returns `True` unconditionally ("Todo tool has no external requirements -- always available"), so there is no provider or model gate of the kind that constrains gemini-cli's `write_todos`.

### daemon_capability: bug

A trace EXISTS in the source the daemon already reads, but the hermes adapter discards it, so the load-bearing observable — three items in the session API `tasks` field with matching subjects and status — is never produced.

What the store holds: a completed `todo` invocation lands as two rows in `$HERMES_HOME/state.db`'s `messages` table — an `assistant` row whose `tool_calls` column carries the OpenAI-shaped call INCLUDING `function.arguments` (the `todos[]` snapshot), and a `tool` row whose `content` is `todo_tool`'s return value, `{"todos": [...], "summary": {...}}` — the full current list. Verified against a live store (11 sessions / 117 message rows at `/Users/ingo/hermes-local/.hermes/state.db`): every `tool_calls` row persists arguments verbatim, e.g. `[{"id": "888148639", "call_id": "888148639", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "terminal", "arguments": "{\"command\":\"ls ...\"}"}}]`, and the paired `role='tool'` row carries the result payload.

What the adapter does with it: `core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/parser.go`'s `parseToolCalls` (lines 118–145) unmarshals each call into a struct with only `ID`, `CallID` and `Function.Name` and emits `tailer.ToolUse{ID, Name}` — `function.arguments` is not in the struct at all, so the `todos[]` snapshot is dropped at parse time. `ParseLine` never sets `TaskDeltas` or `TaskSnapshot`. Downstream, `metrics.go`'s `querySessionMetrics` (lines 124–173) and `messageFold.apply` (lines 227–249) fold only `openTools`, `lastAssistantText` and the waiting cue — neither `metrics.Tasks` nor `metrics.AppliedTaskDeltas` is ever assigned (`grep -rn Tasks core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/` returns nothing). So the session API's `tasks` field stays nil for every hermes session, and `SessionDetector.recordTaskDeltas` (`core/application/services/session_detector_activity.go:746`, which iterates `state.Metrics.AppliedTaskDeltas`) records ZERO `task_delta` lifecycle events.

This is a parser/metrics gap, not architectural incapability: the same signal, on the same `agent.ProcessOwnedStore` transport, is already handled for opencode — `core/adapters/inbound/agents/opencode/parser.go:276` (`appendTodowriteDeltas`) turns each full-list snapshot into TaskDeltas plus a `TaskSnapshot`, and `metrics.go:159` assigns `metrics.Tasks = tasks`. Hermes' `todo` has the same full-list-replace shape AND, unlike gemini-cli's `write_todos`, carries a stable per-item `id`, so the reconciliation is id-keyed rather than content-keyed — strictly simpler than the opencode port it would copy.

The rest of the scenario IS observable today. `finish_reason` is an explicit turn boundary (`parser.go:93` maps `assistant`/`stop` to `turn_done`; the watcher's `turnIsDone`, `watcher.go:426`, marks the activity event Terminal), so ready → working → ready settles without an idle heuristic, and the intervening `todo` calls hold the session in `working` via the open-tool-call set. No child session is created, so `SubagentCount` stays 0.

### driver_capability: ready

The recipe needs `send`, `wait_turn` and `sleep`. All three are genuinely ported in `replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh`: `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`, `send_text` types the literal text then Enter after a 0.4s beat, and `wait_turn` (SEAM 2) polls the store for `COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id=... AND role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop'` exceeding `EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN` — a real signal poll on Hermes' explicit turn marker, not an idle guess. Launch is `hermes chat` under tmux with `wait_for_prompt` polling for the ready banner. No stubbed arm (`interrupt`, `keys`, `reset_session`, `restart`, `resume`, `sigkill`, `exit_clean`, `start_session`, `session`) is required by this recipe.

Interactive rather than headless deliberately: Hermes' one-shot `-z` mode exits at turn completion, so the process would not outlive the daemon's observation window and the settle phase would validate as missing.

## Recording notes

Hermes is a presession adapter for spec-anchoring purposes: it declares a `ProcessMatcher` (`agent.go:32-36`), so `processlifecycle`'s scanner mints a transient `proc-<PID>` row at launch, while the real `sessions` row — and therefore the real session id, shaped `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>` — is INSERTed only on the first user message, ~2s later (`adapter.go` package doc). The spec therefore models the birth as two phases and anchors every later phase to the real session, per the presession template.
caveats: The 117-row sample store carries no `todo` call yet (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE tool_calls LIKE '%"todo"%'` → 0), so the exact persisted shape of a todo call is INFERRED from the terminal/kanban/read_file calls in that store, which do carry function.arguments verbatim, plus todo_tool.py's return value. `record` promotes this from provisional to settled.

A fix that mirrors opencode exactly would close the API-surface half but NOT the `task_tracked` phase: opencode's ProcessOwnedStore path assigns `metrics.Tasks` but never `metrics.AppliedTaskDeltas` (grep: the only writers of AppliedTaskDeltas are core/pkg/tailer/tailer.go:977,1024), so opencode records no `task_delta` events either. The hermes fix should populate both — Tasks for the API field, AppliedTaskDeltas so the observable is assertable in events.jsonl (#662).

`model` and `cost` are deliberately left unpinned in observations. The recording home's model is a human choice, and irrlicht prices hermes via its own alias table rather than the store's `estimated_cost_usd` (which the local store reports as 0.0 under subscription billing): the locally configured `gpt-5.6-luna` has no entry in core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go, and EstimateCostUSD returns 0 for an unpriced model (core/pkg/capacity/capacity.go:159-162), so a `cost_nonzero` assertion would fail for reasons unrelated to this scenario. `tokens_nonzero` is safe — the sessions row carries input/output token aggregates (observed 16269/5 on a live row).

`hermes chat` records `source='cli'`, and Hermes populates `sessions.cwd` only from its TUI gateway, so the session's project binding comes from the live-process CWD fallback (watcher.go:115-124 / metrics.go:120-122), which returns "" when zero or more than one hermes session process is alive. A concurrent hermes session during recording would leave the cell's cwd unbound; not asserted by this spec, but it affects project-dir attribution.

sources.note: TODO_SCHEMA name="todo", items {id, content, status}, VALID_STATUSES pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled, merge=false is a full-list replace, registry.register(name="todo", toolset="todo"), check_todo_requirements() always True.
"todo" is in the default CLI tool list ("# Planning & memory"), its own `todo` toolset, and the `coding` + `hermes-acp` toolsets — enabled by default on the surfaces this cell records.

parseToolCalls unmarshals only {id, call_id, function.name} — function.arguments (the todos[] snapshot) is not in the struct, so it is dropped at parse time. ParseLine sets no TaskDeltas/TaskSnapshot.
querySessionMetrics and messageFold.apply never assign metrics.Tasks or metrics.AppliedTaskDeltas; `grep -rn Tasks core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/` returns no matches at all.
recordTaskDeltas emits one task_delta lifecycle event per state.Metrics.AppliedTaskDeltas entry — with the slice never populated for hermes, events.jsonl carries zero task_delta events.

The reference fix on the SAME ProcessOwnedStore transport: appendTodowriteDeltas converts a full-list snapshot into TaskDeltas + TaskSnapshot, metrics.go assigns metrics.Tasks. Hermes' todo carries a stable per-item id, so its port is id-keyed rather than content-keyed.

Live store, 11 sessions / 117 message rows. `SELECT tool_calls FROM messages WHERE tool_calls IS NOT NULL LIMIT 1` shows function.arguments persisted verbatim; `SELECT role, tool_name, content FROM messages WHERE role='tool'` shows the tool result payload persisted. `SELECT COUNT(*) ... LIKE '%"todo"%'` → 0 (no todo call recorded yet).

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"; send_text, wait_turn (store poll on finish_reason='stop') and the launch/wait_for_prompt seams are ported — the stubbed arms this recipe never reaches are interrupt/keys/reset_session/restart/resume/sigkill/exit_clean/start_session/session.

ProcessMatcher declared (so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession), while the real sessions row is INSERTed ~2s after launch on the first user message — the presession/real-session split the spec's two-phase birth is anchored to.

recipe.prompt: Use your todo tool to create exactly three todo items, in this order: 'read README', 'summarize README', 'reply done'. Then work them one at a time: for each item call todo again to set that item's status to in_progress, then call todo again to set it to completed, before moving on to the next one. Keep everything in this one session - do NOT use delegate_task or spawn any subagent. When all three items are completed, reply with exactly the word: done
verify: state.db messages contains assistant rows whose tool_calls carry function.name='todo' with a todos[] snapshot walking the three items 'read README' / 'summarize README' / 'reply done' from pending through in_progress to completed
no delegate_task call and no child session row (parent_session_id stays NULL); SubagentCount stays 0

the session API tasks field lists the three items with matching subjects, all ending completed (KNOWN FAILING - the hermes parser drops function.arguments and populates neither Tasks nor AppliedTaskDeltas)
state follows ready -> working -> ready; final session state is ready
